summary: No tested combination satisfies every originally frozen criterion (see criteria); the explicit 2026-07-27 product re-judgment revises the realtime RTF gate on a documented machine baseline and approves x-asr-160ms realtime plus offline X-ASR refinement (see rejudgment).

evidence.note: The tracked CLI observations are path-free; raw local logs are ignored and linked per run by rawOutputSha256.

punctuationPresent.evidence: X-ASR 480ms emitted commas on official code-switch samples and the controlled code-switch case.

codeSwitchDoesNotCrash.evidence: All X-ASR candidates exited successfully; X-ASR 480ms preserved the controlled Chinese/English content.

firstPartialLatency.target: P95 < 1000 ms from detected speech onset

refinementBenefit.target: macro CER delta > 0 with no unreported regression

archives.note: Offline non-streaming X-ASR transducer; refinement candidate evaluated in M3 and approved by the 2026-07-27 re-judgment.
The archive contains float/int8 and multiple chunk variants; the selected top-level int8 model files total about 50 MB.

rejudgment.context: The M2 sweep proved both frozen failures are architectural, not tunable: x-asr-480ms needs 960-980 ms of audio before its first token on the Chinese/code-switch cases regardless of threads, and x-asr-160ms bottoms out at RTF 0.47 official / 0.50 controlled at numThreads=4. The product owner explicitly re-set the RTF gate instead of silently relaxing it.

realtimeRtf.revised: < 0.60 per official sample on the approval machine baseline
realtimeRtf.rationale: The 0.35 line was margin for weak machines plus dual-source capture plus refinement headroom. On the documented baseline (Intel Core Ultra 9 185H, 16 cores / 22 threads) the measured worst case is 0.50; dual-source concurrency uses 2x4 of 22 threads and the approved offline refinement adds only RTF 0.027. 0.60 keeps a measured margin on this baseline; weaker machines are NOT covered by this approval and must not receive the profile without their own benchmark.

firstPartialLatency.target: P95 < 1000 ms from detected speech onset
firstPartialLatency.evidence: Full-corpus t=4 bench measured 2026-07-27 during this re-judgment (x160FirstPartialBench in gate-0b-m2-sweep.json): code-switch P95 697.5 ms, en-onboarding 709.0 ms, zh-roadmap 855.8 ms all pass; zh-date-itn P95 1000.3 ms (P50 992.4 ms) rides the frozen line because the utterance needs exactly 960 ms of audio before the first token in all 5 runs - the same utterance-dependent floor x-asr-480ms shows on this case. Not rounded to pass; recorded as a marginal case.

knownLimitations: x-asr-160ms emits little or no punctuation on the short controlled utterances (macro punctuation F1 0 on the controlled corpus at t=4); punctuation recovery is delegated to the approved refinement pass, so refinement must be enabled for final captions by default.
numThreads >= 6 regresses RTF on the hybrid P/E-core architecture and must not be used.

First-partial latency is utterance-dependent: openings that give the model little early phonetic evidence (zh-date-itn) sit at a ~960 ms audio floor, so occasional first-caption delays of ~1.0 s will occur; typical cases are ~0.7-0.86 s. x-asr-480ms hits the same floor on such cases while also being >= 980 ms on the common ones.

criteria.target: no content regression and a measurable net benefit over the realtime baseline
criteria.evidence: Zero content regression on both baselines (macro CER 0 -> 0, 0 regressed cases) and punctuation F1 restored from 0.1667 (x480) / 0.0 (x160-t4) to 1.0000; SenseVoice failed exactly these two criteria.

tradeoffs: Japanese/Korean/Cantonese refinement capability is lost with SenseVoice; the product currently only promises zh/en.
Disk: ~168 MB extracted, replacing SenseVoice's ~230 MB (first-run download budget improves).

standingConditions: This approval is scoped to the documented machine baseline; packaged builds (B5/I4) must re-benchmark on target machines before publishing the fast profile there, and machines that fail stay at availableProfiles [].
The controlled corpus remains clean deterministic SAPI speech (4 cases); multi-speaker, far-field, noisy and real-accent corpus expansion stays an open obligation before widening quality claims.
The original 0.35 criterion stays recorded above; any further model or threshold change requires a new explicit product decision against the same frozen benchmark scripts.

decision.action: Publish the fast profile only where the runtime matches the re-judgment machine baseline; keep every other profile unavailable and re-run the frozen benchmark before any further model or threshold change.

limitations: Controlled accuracy uses deterministic SAPI voices, not a multi-speaker noisy meeting corpus.
First-partial latency uses five paced runs per 40 ms case and a -45 dBFS speech-onset detector on one development machine.
The official CLI archive contains no sherpa-onnx-microphone.exe, so microphone latency was measured with the matching v1.13.4 Node N-API binding.
CLI success validates model selection only; Electron utility-process integration remains a later backend gate.
